sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A population has 257 shoppers at a grocery store. Student A takes a random sample of 5. Student B takes a random sample of 63. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Student A's sample of 5, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student B's sample of 63, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.

items.prompt: A student surveys 25 visitors to a science museum using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 475 visitors to a science museum?
choices: Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.

items.prompt: A sample of 6 values is: 27, 25, 15, 13, 13, 20. What is the range of this data set?
A data set has 5 values: 24, 20, 21, 23, 20. What is the new mean if an outlier of 47 is added to the data set, making 6 values in all?
A data set is: 39, 14, 21, 17, 49, with a mean of 28. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 71 and 99. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 7. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 3 times the MAD
4 times the MAD
8 times the MAD
6 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 27, 31, 30, 39, 43, 40. Sample B: 62, 61, 66, 59, 52, 42. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample B, with a mean of 35 compared to 57.
Both samples have the same mean.
Sample A, with a mean of 35 compared to 57.
Sample B, with a mean of 57 compared to 35.

items.prompt: Sample A: 45, 53, 47, 51, 49, 51. Sample B: 59, 41, 57, 62, 45, 64. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample B, with a range of 23 compared to 8.
Sample A, with a range of 23 compared to 8.
Sample A, with a range of 8 compared to 23.
Both samples have the same range.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 504 commuters on a train line. She randomly selects 111 of them to survey. What is the population in this situation?
choices: All 504 commuters on a train line
Only the first 111 commuters on a train line on a list
The 111 randomly selected commuters on a train line
The researcher's own estimate

items.prompt: A student picks a random starting point, then surveys every 10th person from the full numbered list of shoppers at a grocery store, for a total of 27. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.
No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 37 shoppers at a grocery store, 30 preferred a new park design. Based on this sample, about how many of the 259 shoppers at a grocery store would you expect to prefer a new park design?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 19, 17, 18, 18, 15. What is the range of these sample estimates?
